root_cause.text: In the RDMA/rxe MR mapping code, iova-to-VA translation incorrectly assumed each `page_list` entry represented one `mr->page_size` page, even though the xarray stored only `struct page *` at system `PAGE_SIZE` granularity and no per-page offset, causing wrong index/offset calculations when `mr->page_size != PAGE_SIZE`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states that “rxe_set_page() is called with `mr->page_size` step increments, but the page_list stores individual struct page pointers, each representing `PAGE_SIZE` of memory,” and the patch fixes this by replacing `page_list` with `struct rxe_mr_page { struct page *page; unsigned int offset; }`, adding separate index/offset conversion for `mr->page_size > PAGE_SIZE` and `<= PAGE_SIZE`, and using `page_offset += info->offset` during accesses.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix MR IOVA-to-page_info index and offset translation for non-PAGE_SIZE-aligned and larger-than-PAGE_SIZE memory regions, with an added bounds warning.
intent_record.what: The change adds explanatory comments and rewrites rxe_mr_iova_to_index() and rxe_mr_iova_to_page_offset() to handle two cases based on whether mr_page_size(mr) is greater than PAGE_SIZE. In rxe_mr_iova_to_index(), a local idx variable is introduced; for MR page sizes larger than PAGE_SIZE, the index is computed from iova relative to (mr->ibmr.iova & mr->page_mask) using PAGE_SHIFT, otherwise the original page_shift-based calculation is retained. A WARN_ON(idx >= mr->nbuf) check is also added before returning idx. In rxe_mr_iova_to_page_offset(), the offset calculation now uses PAGE_SIZE - 1 when mr_page_size(mr) > PAGE_SIZE, otherwise it keeps using mr_page_size(mr) - 1.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this fixes address-to-buffer mapping for memory regions whose configured page size is larger than the system PAGE_SIZE, especially when the MR IOVA is not aligned to the MR page size. It ensures the correct page_info entry and in-page offset are derived for both larger-than-system and smaller-or-equal page sizes, preventing incorrect indexing into mr->page_info and catching out-of-range indices with a warning.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace xarray-backed MR page storage with an allocated page_info array and add allocation/free helpers while preserving SG page population and persistent-page validation.
intent_record.what: The change rewrites rxe_mr_fill_pages_from_sgt() to stop using an xarray-based page_list insertion loop and instead iterate the scatterlist pages directly into mr->page_info[mr->nbuf], setting each entry's page and offset, incrementing nbuf, returning -EINVAL immediately for non-pmem pages when persistent access is requested, and returning 0 on success. It also adds a WARN_ON that mr_page_size(mr) equals PAGE_SIZE, and introduces three new helpers: __alloc_mr_page_info() to allocate and initialize mr->page_info, alloc_mr_page_info() to wrap allocation and set mr->num_buf with a WARN_ON if already set, and free_mr_page_info() to free and clear mr->page_info.
intent_record.how: At runtime, MR page tracking now uses a contiguous allocated page_info array instead of storing pages in an xarray, so SG pages are recorded sequentially with explicit buffer count bookkeeping. This removes the previous xarray lock/store/error/nomem retry path, makes persistent-memory validation fail immediately before storing any invalid page, and provides explicit allocation and teardown routines for the page metadata storage used by the MR.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant page_list xarray initialization from rxe_mr_init_user() because that setup is handled elsewhere.
intent_record.what: The call to xa_init(&mr->page_list) was removed from rxe_mr_init_user() immediately after rxe_mr_init(access, mr) and before ib_umem_get().
intent_record.how: At runtime, rxe_mr_init_user() no longer explicitly initializes mr->page_list at that point, implying the xarray is expected to already be initialized elsewhere or is no longer needed there; this avoids redundant or misplaced initialization during user memory region setup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Allocate MR page metadata during user MR initialization and add proper cleanup on failure to prevent incomplete setup and resource leaks.
intent_record.what: In rxe_mr_init_user(), the change adds a call to alloc_mr_page_info(mr, ib_umem_num_pages(umem)) after successful umem acquisition, checks its return value, and introduces error labels so that failures in either alloc_mr_page_info() or rxe_mr_fill_pages_from_sgt() clean up with free_mr_page_info(mr) and ib_umem_release(umem). At the same time, the previously separate static helper rxe_mr_alloc() is removed from this location.
intent_record.how: At runtime, user MR initialization now allocates MR page metadata before populating pages from the scatter-gather table, ensuring the required page-info structure exists. If page population fails, the newly allocated page info is freed before releasing umem, preventing leaked MR page state and making initialization failure handling complete and consistent.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the page info allocation helper during fast MR initialization so fast memory regions are set up with the correct allocation path.
intent_record.what: In rxe_mr_init_fast(), the call assigning err was changed from rxe_mr_alloc(mr, max_pages) to alloc_mr_page_info(mr, max_pages), while the surrounding error handling and control flow remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, fast MR initialization now uses a page-info-specific allocation routine instead of the previous generic MR allocation function, changing the resource setup performed for mr during initialization while preserving the existing failure path if allocation returns an error.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix rxe_set_page() to correctly track MR mappings at system-page granularity, including large-page splitting, sub-page offsets, and proper bounds and persistent-page checks.
intent_record.what: The function rxe_set_page() was rewritten to stop storing a single page in mr->page_list via xa_store() and instead iterate over one or more PAGE_SIZE chunks derived from dma_addr, computing pages_per_mr as max(1, mr_page_size(mr) >> PAGE_SHIFT). For each chunk it now translates the adjusted address to a struct page, checks mr->nbuf against mr->max_allowed_buf, validates persistent mappings per sub-page, stores the page and its PAGE_SIZE-relative offset into mr->page_info[mr->nbuf], and increments mr->nbuf. A descriptive comment was also added explaining handling for MRs with page sizes greater than or less than PAGE_SIZE.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now correctly records memory regions whose MR page size may be larger than a system page by splitting them into multiple PAGE_SIZE entries, and also preserves offsets for MR page sizes smaller than PAGE_SIZE. This prevents incorrect one-entry-per-call bookkeeping, enforces the proper buffer limit with max_allowed_buf, and ensures persistent-memory validation is applied to each actual system page being tracked.

intent_record.intent_summary: Validate MR page-size compatibility with PAGE_SIZE and resize page_info for large MR pages to prevent invalid mappings and insufficient buffer allocation.
intent_record.what: The change adds two validation/allocation blocks at the start of rxe_map_mr_sg(): first, it checks that mr page_size and PAGE_SIZE are compatible by requiring either page_size to be aligned to PAGE_SIZE or PAGE_SIZE to be aligned to page_size, logging a debug message and returning -EINVAL otherwise; second, when mr_page_size(mr) is greater than PAGE_SIZE, it computes a larger required page_info size as (page_size >> PAGE_SHIFT) * mr->num_buf, compares it against mr->max_allowed_buf, logs and frees existing page info, and reallocates it with __alloc_mr_page_info(), returning -ENOMEM on allocation failure.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents mapping with incompatible memory-region page sizes that would break address-to-page conversion, and it ensures the page_info backing storage is expanded when the MR uses pages larger than the kernel base page size so the mapping logic has enough entries; this avoids invalid mappings and potential buffer sizing failures during SG mapping.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix rxe_mr_copy_xarray() to recompute page mapping from IOVA each iteration and use page_info offsets so MR copies access the correct backing pages.
intent_record.what: The function rxe_mr_copy_xarray() was changed to recompute the page index and page offset from iova on each loop iteration instead of initializing them once and incrementing index manually. It now uses mr->page_info[index] to obtain a struct rxe_mr_page, checks info->page instead of xa_load(&mr->page_list, index), adds info->offset to the computed page offset, limits the copy size by PAGE_SIZE - page_offset instead of mr_page_size(mr) - page_offset, maps info->page with kmap_local_page(), removes the page_offset reset and index increment, and advances iova by bytes each iteration.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the copy now follows the current IOVA position across iterations and uses per-page metadata from page_info, including an additional page-specific offset, to access the correct backing page and byte range. This fixes incorrect traversal and sizing when memory regions are not represented as simple contiguous mr-sized pages, preventing copies from reading or writing the wrong page locations and avoiding faults or data corruption from using stale index/offset calculations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused local variables from rxe_mr_flush_pmem_iova() to clean up dead code and silence compiler warnings.
intent_record.what: The change removes three local variable declarations from rxe_mr_flush_pmem_iova(): an unsigned int page_offset, an unsigned long index, and a struct page *page, while leaving the remaining local variables unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime this does not change execution behavior directly; it eliminates unused local variables from the function, reducing dead code and avoiding possible compiler warnings about unused declarations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix pmem MR flushing to use per-page metadata offsets and the correct backing page when issuing cache writeback.
intent_record.what: Inside the flush loop, the code changes from loading a page directly from mr->page_list via xa_load() to deriving an index, taking a struct rxe_mr_page entry from mr->page_info[index], and using that entry's page and offset fields. It adds local declarations for index and page_offset inside the loop, replaces the null check from !page to !info->page, adjusts page_offset by adding info->offset, computes bytes using PAGE_SIZE - page_offset instead of mr_page_size(mr) - page_offset, and maps info->page instead of page.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the flush now operates on the actual backing page and intra-page offset recorded in mr->page_info rather than assuming a direct page lookup with offsets relative only to the MR page size. This ensures the pmem cache writeback targets the correct physical page region, including sub-page offsets, and limits flushing to the remaining bytes in the underlying PAGE_SIZE page, preventing incorrect address calculation during pmem flush.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a local `rxe_mr_page` pointer in `rxe_mr_do_atomic_op()` to support later page-level handling in the non-direct access path.
intent_record.what: A new local variable declaration, `struct rxe_mr_page *info;`, was added inside the `else` branch of `rxe_mr_do_atomic_op()` alongside the existing `index` and `err` declarations.
intent_record.how: At runtime this change by itself does not alter control flow or behavior in the shown hunk, but it prepares the function to store or access a memory-region page descriptor within that branch, likely for subsequent page-based operations added elsewhere in the function.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix atomic MR access to use `page_info` metadata so page lookup and effective offsets are computed correctly.
intent_record.what: The code stops loading a page directly from `mr->page_list` with `xa_load(&mr->page_list, index)` and instead retrieves `info = &mr->page_info[index]`, checks `info->page` for null, adds `info->offset` to `page_offset`, and assigns `page = info->page`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, atomic memory operations now use per-index page metadata from `mr->page_info`, including an additional stored offset, rather than only the raw page pointer from the xarray. This prevents operations from proceeding when the mapped page metadata is missing and fixes address translation within the page when a nonzero per-page offset is required.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a local `rxe_mr_page` pointer in `rxe_mr_do_atomic_write()` to support upcoming page-handling logic in the atomic write path.
intent_record.what: A new local variable declaration, `struct rxe_mr_page *info;`, was added inside the `else` block of `rxe_mr_do_atomic_write()` alongside the existing `index` and `err` declarations.
intent_record.how: At runtime this enables the function to reference an `rxe_mr_page` pointer within that code path, likely supporting subsequent page-related logic added nearby, but this hunk alone does not show any direct behavior change.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use `page_info` metadata for atomic writes so the correct page and adjusted offset are used, fixing invalid or misplaced memory access.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a direct page lookup via `xa_load(&mr->page_list, index)` and null check on `page` with access to `mr->page_info[index]`, checks `info->page` instead, adds `page_offset += info->offset`, and assigns `page = info->page`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, atomic writes now use per-index page metadata from `page_info`, including an additional stored offset, rather than assuming the IOVA-derived page offset alone is sufficient; this prevents accessing a missing page through the old lookup path and ensures the write targets the correct backing page location when pages have associated offsets.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the dedicated page-info cleanup helper for non-DMA memory regions so all associated page metadata is properly released during rxe_mr_cleanup().
intent_record.what: In rxe_mr_cleanup(), the cleanup path for memory regions whose ibmr.type is not IB_MR_TYPE_DMA was changed from directly calling xa_destroy(&mr->page_list) to calling free_mr_page_info(mr).
intent_record.how: At runtime, non-DMA memory region cleanup now uses a dedicated helper instead of only destroying the xarray, which likely frees the full page-related metadata associated with the memory region rather than just tearing down the page_list container, preventing incomplete resource cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a helper structure to represent a memory page and its offset for future RXE memory-region handling.
intent_record.what: A new struct type named rxe_mr_page was added before struct rxe_mr, containing a struct page pointer field named page and an unsigned int field named offset with a comment indicating it stores the offset within a system page.
intent_record.how: This introduces a new data representation for tracking a memory page together with its in-page offset, enabling later code to store or pass both pieces of page-related state as a single object; by itself, this hunk does not change runtime behavior until the new struct is used.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace xarray-based MR page storage with direct page_info tracking and add explicit fields for allocated versus allowed page buffer counts.
intent_record.what: The struct rxe_mr definition was changed by adding two comments, introducing a new u32 field named max_allowed_buf after num_buf, and replacing the page_list member of type struct xarray with a page_info member of type struct rxe_mr_page *.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes the memory region structure from storing page metadata in an xarray to storing it through a direct page_info pointer, while also tracking both the allocated page_info size and the actual allowed size via num_buf and max_allowed_buf. This enables different bookkeeping for MR page storage and capacity management.

This group introduces exactly that page-and-offset abstraction (`rxe_mr_page` and related handling scaffolding) in RXE MR code, which is directly aligned with fixing the incorrect assumption that each entry mapped one full `mr->page_size` page.

candidates.rationale: This computes the backing-page index using MR page_shift, implicitly assuming each page_list entry corresponds to one MR-sized page. That is the core faulty translation when page_list actually stores struct page entries at PAGE_SIZE granularity.

This bounds copy length by MR page size after selecting a PAGE_SIZE-granularity struct page, reinforcing the wrong assumption that each loaded page_list entry spans an MR-sized page.

vuln_statements.explanation: This computes the xarray lookup index in units of mr->page_size, assuming each page_list entry corresponds to one MR-sized page. The root cause is that page_list actually stores struct page * entries at PAGE_SIZE granularity, so this translation becomes wrong when mr->page_size != PAGE_SIZE.

This computes the intra-page offset using the MR page size rather than the actual PAGE_SIZE granularity of the stored struct page entries. Without per-entry offset metadata, this yields incorrect VA offsets when mr->page_size differs from PAGE_SIZE.

This stores only a bare struct page * at index mr->nbuf, with no offset or subpage metadata. That storage format is incompatible with later MR-page-based index and offset calculations, creating the granularity mismatch at the heart of the vulnerability.

This retrieves a page_list entry using the incorrectly computed MR-page-based index. Because page_list entries are actually PAGE_SIZE-based struct page mappings, the lookup can return the wrong backing page when mr->page_size != PAGE_SIZE.

This copy-length bound uses MR page size after selecting a PAGE_SIZE-granularity struct page entry, reinforcing the incorrect assumption that each page_list entry spans an MR-sized page and contributing to wrong address translation/copy behavior.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes the new iova-to-index/offset translation helpers and all xarray-based access paths that use them. The vulnerable construct is present in the new xarray implementation. Specifically, `rxe_mr_iova_to_index()` returns `(iova >> mr->page_shift) - (mr->ibmr.iova >> mr->page_shift);` and `rxe_mr_iova_to_page_offset()` returns `iova & (mr_page_size(mr) - 1);`. These calculations use `mr->page_shift` / `mr_page_size(mr)` as if each xarray entry corresponds to one MR page of size `mr->page_size`. But the xarray is populated with plain `struct page *` entries at system page granularity: in `rxe_mr_fill_pages_from_sgt()` it iterates sg pages and does `xas_store(&xas, page); xas_next(&xas);`, one xarray slot per `struct page *`; likewise in `rxe_set_page()` it stores `page = virt_to_page(iova & mr->page_mask);` via `xa_store(&mr->page_list, mr->nbuf, page, GFP_KERNEL)`. There is no per-entry offset or representation of larger-than-PAGE_SIZE MR pages. Yet readers such as `rxe_mr_copy_xarray()` do `index = rxe_mr_iova_to_index(mr, iova);`, `page = xa_load(&mr->page_list, index);`, and then compute `bytes = min_t(..., mr_page_size(mr) - page_offset);` and access `va + page_offset`. `rxe_flush_pmem_iova()`, `rxe_mr_do_atomic_op()`, and `rxe_mr_do_atomic_write()` use the same helpers and assumptions. Therefore, when `mr->page_size != PAGE_SIZE`, index and offset are derived using MR-page granularity while storage is at PAGE_SIZE granularity, matching the stated root cause. No fix is present in this snippet: there is no translation based on `PAGE_SIZE`, no storage of offsets, and no logic reconciling xarray slot granularity with `mr->page_size`.
